design.scope: Only Gaussian neighborhood-size comparison on 4 reference images, upper/lower structure; no Huber/line/theta tests.
design.paper_comparison: Fabijanska 2015 Fig.3/Table1 compares fixed-position fits across odd N=3..21. Report every position rather than selecting one example to decide for the whole structure.
design.expanded_sample_counts: N=23..61 extends the previously discussed range. This upper endpoint is a tested range, not a stability criterion or universal bound.
design.coarse_selection: Existing signed-positive Gy maximum in each existing search band. Earliest y resolves exact ties. All visible columns at 1px spacing.
design.unchanged_spatial_scope: Same x range, y band, and central occlusion masks as the previous experiment. Samples may extend beyond the coarse-search band; all are real source pixels.
design.gradient: Native OpenCV 3.4.15; full-image raw grayscale Sobel dy=1,dx=0,ksize=3,scale=1,border=REFLECT101; polarity=+1.
design.model: A exp(-(y-mu)^2/(2 sigma^2)), raw signed samples, unweighted SSE, no offset. Existing numerical abs(sigma)+1e-12 retained.
design.initialization: 2014 predecessor III.B: A=max response of the fitted neighborhood, mu=coarse location, sigma=N. Unlike the earlier experiment, initial sigma is not fixed at 11.
design.solver: Existing exact Nelder-Mead source; initial simplex steps=.2*A,1,.5*N; max800 and relative objective-spread tolerance1e-10. These numerical settings are inherited implementation choices, not specified/validated by the 2015 paper. All returns retained.
design.reporting: Every attempted fit saved, including nonfinite and nonconverged results; solver status is recorded, not used to hide rows. No extra position bounds, clipping, outlier removal, peak-count test, or residual gate.
design.selection: No invented px threshold, acceptance percentage, or smallest-stable-N rule. Full tables and all-position changes are inspected. A sample count will not be forced if the unfiltered results do not support it.
